To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The pBR322 origin of replication is sequestered by the SeqA protein.
the SeqA gene product can regulate the replication initiation of the pBR 322 plasmid by direct DNA binding.
the SeqA gene product binds exclusively to the RNA II promoter of the pBR 322 plasmid in a hemimethylate-dependent manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Seq A protein in the control of the replication of pBR322 plamid.
the role of Seq A in the regulation of the initiation of replication.
the study of the regulation of replication of pBR322 plasimid and the role of Seq A protein in this control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SeqA is a hemimethyl-specific protein which can recognize the hemimethyl form of the pBR plasmid and oriC.
SeqA protein is involved in the regulation of pBR322 plasid replication.
SeqA is an important factor for the control of pBR322 replication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the replication initiation of the pBR32 plasmid is controlled by the methylation state and by the SeqA protein.
SeqA is involved in the regulation of the pBR plasmid replication and the host origin ori C.
SeqA protein could regulate periodically the initiation of the pBR plasmid replication, by binding to its origin sequence in a hemimethylate state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SeqA could be a universal protein that can regulate the initiation of replication for different plasmids.
the pBR322 RNA II promoter region is regulated by adenine methylation and that the SeqA gene product is involved in the regulation of the pBR332 RNAII promoter region.
the regulation of pBR322 RNA II promoter by SeqA protein is similar to ori C regulation by SeqA protein.
